processing: Details for this cultivar are little documented. Typical of Sichuan early greens, the fresh shoots are spread, fixed, shaped and dried without oxidation.
harvest_season: Not well documented for this cultivar. Sichuan green teas are generally prized at the earliest spring picking.
appearance_dry: No reliable description exists for this cultivar; Sichuan early greens are usually slim, bud-heavy and fresh green.
appearance_liquor: As with other Sichuan early greens, expect a pale, clear yellow-green.
appearance_wet: As with other bud-picked Sichuan greens, expect tender, bright green shoots.
taste_profile: No documented tasting profile for this cultivar. Sichuan early greens in general run fresh, lightly vegetal and gently sweet.

brewing.notes: A general approach for tender Chinese greens, in a glass or gaiwan with water well off the boil.

vintage_note: A cultivar name, seldom a retail label. Like other Chinese greens, tea from it would be sold as the current spring harvest and is best drunk within the year.
description:
Chuancha No. 2 is a named tea cultivar from Sichuan, one of ten local cultivars bred in Leshan City. It is a plant variety first of all, so you are more likely to meet it in a breeder's list than on a shop shelf.

Little has been published in the open about its leaf, its picking date or how it behaves in the cup. Anything about flavour here is what is usual for Sichuan early greens, not a measured trait of this plant: a fresh, lightly vegetal cup with a soft sweetness.

If you do find it named on a bag, brew it gently as you would any tender green, with cooler water and no long first steep. Ask the seller which year and which picking it is, since the season matters at least as much as the cultivar.
history: Chuancha No. 2 is listed in a 2024 review in the journal China Tea among ten cultivars bred in Leshan, next to Emei Wenchun and Chuancha No. 3 and No. 10. Who bred it, from which parents and in which year is little documented in openly available material.
sources_note: Master row placed it in Yibin; the only source read ties it to Leshan, so region was changed. Category green is assumed from the row.
